title: His first marijuana, at fifteen, at a Dallas football game
summary: His cousin Sharpie's habit and a band trip to Dallas led to his first marijuana.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Yeah, that's what broke us up. Because
I had been addicted when I was fifteen.

Yeah. For an elder cousin of mine that I admired, he was a young man of the streets, you know. And I'd always like to ride with him when I'd get out of school. He was always going around with these pretty girls, their house and blowing his horn, you know. I'd say I'm going to be like him when I grow up, you know. All these pretty girls you know. So I had an occasion to go to Dallas to this football game. Did I mention anything about that?
I think I said I went to Dallas to the football game. I couldn't play football, so I went with the band.

Oh well, anyway, if I didn't I'll repeat myself. Carmyte? [Mike] Thompson was playing the dance in the Elks Hall, so I run into a violin player named T. Moore. He walked up to me, he says 'hey, Jeff,' just like, saying hey man or hey baby or brother. At that time he says 'hey Jeff. Are you hip?' He says all right, come go with me.

So he's got his violin on his arm and goes on down to the pawn shop, pawns his horn, walks in the back of the pawn shop, comes out and we walk about a hundred feet and he opens up this package of marijuana. I say is that what you went

after? He says yeah. I give him a dollar. I say go get me a pack? He went back and got me a pack. Now all of a sudden it hits me "boing", this is what my cousin was doing, he was pushing marijuana to these pretty girls. This is why he was driving around, you know. So he'd get on the train and go on home that night. I turned everybody on in the band. (Laughter). And the cheerleading squad. The girls too. (Laughter). And the men's room was about four feet wide square, you know. Just big enough for you to go in and do your dues and get out, there wasn't room for two people to go in. We were in there, stacked up high, two standing on the toilet stool and two standing. And if you wasn't smoking, you'd get high anyway. Contact, you know. All the smoke in there.

So the assistant football coach came up to me. He says, I know what you all are doing. You better get rid of that stuff before you get back home, you know. I say okay. So I closed my eyes and then I became aware of rhythm. I heard the railroad ties, you know, the sound the train makes. The wheels on the rail. And I found myself keeping time with it.

So when I got back to Oklahoma, I went back into my old thing, riding with my cousin. So first stop I made, he lit up and I started laughing, he said what you laughing about? I say I know what you doing, man. He say what am I doing? I say you smoking those reefer. Well see, in Oklahoma they had added an R to it, not reefer, but greerfer.
Is the same cousin, cousin Thaddeus?
